footprint.intro: [[RO]] What a site engineer needs before they can say yes. Every figure here is measured or marked as unmeasured — none of it is indicative.
footprint.note: [[RO]] Service clearance is additional to the machine footprint. A site that fits the machine but not the clearance is not a site.

servicing.heading: [[RO]] Servicing
servicing.intro: [[RO]] The part that decides whether this is an asset or a chore. None of it lands on your staff.

items.question: [[RO]] Who empties it?
items.answer: [[RO]] We do. A Green Exchange crew collects on a route driven by fill-level telemetry, not by a calendar and not by a phone call from your duty manager.

items.question: [[RO]] What happens when it jams?
items.answer: [[RO]] The machine reports the fault itself and takes itself out of service so it cannot swallow another container. Your site contact does not diagnose anything; they do not need a key. We attend.

items.question: [[RO]] What is the uptime commitment?
items.answer: [[RO]] Availability is measured per machine over a stated window and reported to you with the volumes. A machine that is down is our problem and it appears in your report, not just ours.

benefits.heading: [[RO]] What comes back to you
benefits.intro: [[RO]] Four things, in the order a board will ask about them. Two of them are unmeasured, and this page says so rather than borrowing a number from another market.

items.heading: [[RO]] Footfall and dwell
items.body: [[RO]] A deposit point gives a reason to come, and the value returned is redeemable in store. We will not put a figure on this before a pilot measures it at your site — anyone who does is guessing on your behalf.

items.heading: [[RO]] Loyalty integration
items.body: [[RO]] Value can be issued to your existing loyalty scheme instead of a paper voucher, which keeps the redemption inside your basket and inside your data.

items.heading: [[RO]] ESG reporting output
items.body: [[RO]] Volumes by material stream, recovered tonnage, and machine availability, per site, on a fixed cadence — in a form you can put into a disclosure without re-deriving it.

items.heading: [[RO]] Compliance positioning
items.body: [[RO]] Egypt has no national deposit-return scheme today. Operating collection infrastructure before one exists is a materially different position from retrofitting under a deadline, and it is the one we can help you take.

roi.heading: [[RO]] Estimate the scale
roi.intro: [[RO]] Set your own numbers. The model is deliberately simple and every coefficient behind it is listed below, with the source it has to come from.

outputs.benefit: [[RO]] Estimated benefit to you per month

roi.disclaimer: [[RO]] These outputs are estimates produced by a model, not a quotation and not a forecast. They are only as good as the assumptions listed below, and they carry no commercial commitment.
assumptions: [[RO]] Every visitor is counted once per day, and a fixed share of visitors deposits containers.
[[RO]] Deposits cannot exceed what the machines on site can physically accept, so throughput caps the result.
[[RO]] The split between PET and aluminium is treated as constant across all sites.
[[RO]] Container mass is an average over the size mix actually returned, not a single container size.
[[RO]] Material value is a spot price per tonne and is volatile; the benefit range does not model that volatility.
[[RO]] Your benefit is a share of recovered material value only. Redemption in store, footfall effects and compliance value are excluded — they are real, and none of them is measured yet.
[[RO]] No capital cost, operating cost or price appears here. Commercial terms are a conversation, not a calculator.
roi.unavailableHeading: [[RO]] This calculator cannot produce a number yet
roi.unavailableBody: [[RO]] The coefficients below have not been measured. Rather than fill them with plausible values, the model reports that it cannot compute. Every input above still works, and the moment a pilot supplies these figures the outputs appear.
roi.throughputNote: [[RO]] At these settings machine throughput is the limit, not footfall — additional visitors would not add containers.

hero.headline: [[RO]] Material recovered, and how we know.
hero.subhead: [[RO]] Impact here means tonnes of PET and aluminium that went back into material rather than to landfill, counted per container at the machine. Every figure below states its unit and the period it covers. Anything not yet measured shows as a dash rather than as a number.

counters.heading: [[RO]] Recovery to date
counters.intro: [[RO]] Cumulative totals from machine telemetry. A figure animates only once it has been measured and has a stated period — until then it is a dash.

flow.heading: [[RO]] Where Egypt’s PET actually goes
flow.intro: [[RO]] The gap this business addresses is not between consumption and recycling — it is between consumption and FORMAL recovery. Informal collectors already recover a large share, and leaving them out of the picture would overstate the problem and misrepresent the market.
flow.title: [[RO]] Egypt PET material flow: consumed against destination
flow.unsourcedHeading: [[RO]] Chart not drawn — no public source
flow.unsourcedBody: [[RO]] The structure of the flow is shown, but not the proportions. Drawing magnitudes without a public source for every band would produce a chart that reads as authoritative and is not. Each band needs a figure from the same study and the same year — mixing sources is how a flow chart ends up looking right and being wrong.
flow.unsourcedDescription: [[RO]] Structure of the Egypt PET material flow: consumption divides into formally collected, informally collected and uncollected. Proportions are not shown because no public source has been supplied.
flow.mismatchHeading: [[RO]] Chart not drawn — bands do not reconcile
flow.mismatchBody: [[RO]] The three destinations do not sum to total consumption within tolerance, which means at least one figure comes from a different study, a different year or a different definition. The chart refuses to draw rather than hide the discrepancy behind rounding.

methodology.heading: [[RO]] How we calculate recovered tonnage
methodology.intro: [[RO]] Short version: we count containers, not bags. Tonnage is derived from counted containers and weighed collections, and the two are reconciled.

steps.heading: [[RO]] Count at the point of acceptance
steps.body: [[RO]] Every accepted container is counted by the machine at the moment it is validated, by material stream. Rejected containers are not counted. This is a count of objects, not an estimate from volume.

steps.heading: [[RO]] Weigh at collection
steps.body: [[RO]] Each collection is weighed by stream when it leaves the site. That gives an actual mass, independent of the container count.

steps.heading: [[RO]] Reconcile the two
steps.body: [[RO]] Counted containers multiplied by the average container mass for that stream should agree with the weighed mass. Where they diverge, the weighed mass is authoritative and the average mass is corrected — not the other way round.

steps.heading: [[RO]] Report the weighed figure
steps.body: [[RO]] Published tonnage is weighed mass, not modelled mass. Contamination and moisture are part of the weighed figure until material is sorted at the processing centre, so the reported figure is conservative rather than flattering.

exclusions.heading: [[RO]] What is deliberately excluded
items: [[RO]] No avoided-emissions figure is published without a stated methodology and a source. A CO₂e number is a calculation, not a measurement, and it inherits every assumption behind it.
[[RO]] No claim is made about material that leaves our custody. We report what we recovered and sold, not what a reprocessor ultimately did with it.
[[RO]] Containers rejected by the machine are excluded entirely, even though a depositor carried them in.

hero.headline: [[RO]] Deposit infrastructure, built before the mandate arrives.
thesis: [[RO]] PET and aluminium enter Egypt in volume and are recovered at a fraction of the rate, because collection depends on informal channels rather than infrastructure.
[[RO]] Retail is where those containers are already carried in and out every day, which makes a store entrance the cheapest place to intercept them.
[[RO]] Regulation is moving toward producer responsibility across the region, and the operators holding retail siting agreements and collection routes when it lands are the ones who can serve it.

market.heading: [[RO]] Market context
market.intro: [[RO]] Four figures matter here, and each appears only when it carries a named public source. Anything unsourced is absent from this page rather than shown with a caveat.
market.pendingHeading: [[RO]] No sourced market figures are published yet
market.pendingBody: [[RO]] The figures for this section have not been tied to a named public source. Rather than publish them with a hedge, they are withheld until each one cites the instrument or dataset it comes from. The full market analysis, with its sources, is in the data room.
market.regulatoryNote: [[RO]] Direction of travel, not a prediction: Egypt legislated a framework for waste management in 2020, and producer-responsibility instruments across MENA have followed the same pattern. We do not model a mandate date, and nothing on this page depends on one arriving.

model.heading: [[RO]] How a machine makes money
model.intro: [[RO]] Four revenue lines. Described as mechanisms only — no figures appear on this page, and the unit economics are in the data room.

lines.heading: [[RO]] Retailer contract
lines.body: [[RO]] The site pays for placement and service, or takes a share of recovered material value, depending on the deal. Either way the machine is contracted per site rather than sold as hardware.

lines.heading: [[RO]] Material sale
lines.body: [[RO]] Baled PET and aluminium are sold to reprocessors. Separation quality upstream sets the price, which is why sorting happens before compaction rather than after.

lines.heading: [[RO]] Brand sponsorship
lines.body: [[RO]] A machine at a store entrance is a branded surface with a measurable interaction count, and beverage producers facing producer-responsibility obligations have a reason to fund collection directly.

lines.heading: [[RO]] Data
lines.body: [[RO]] Every accepted container is a counted, located, time-stamped return by material and by product. That record is what a producer needs to evidence recovery, and it is the line with the lowest marginal cost.

model.note: [[RO]] Which lines carry the model, in what proportion, and at what cost is exactly the question the data room answers. It is not answered here.

traction.heading: [[RO]] Where we actually are
traction.intro: [[RO]] Stated conservatively and stage-appropriately. Built, signed and deployed are separate counts and are kept separate; an unmeasured figure is shown as unmeasured rather than rounded up.
traction.note: [[RO]] A letter of intent is not a pilot and a pilot is not a rollout. Conflating them is the most common way an early company overstates itself, so these are counted separately here.

technology.headline: [[RO]] One container, end to end.
technology.intro: [[RO]] What happens between a depositor putting a bottle in and a reprocessor buying the material back. Each step carries the specification that governs it.

steps.title: [[RO]] Deposit
steps.body: [[RO]] The depositor feeds a single container into the intake. One at a time, upright or on its side — the machine indexes it onto the transport before anything else happens.

steps.title: [[RO]] Identify
steps.body: [[RO]] A barcode read establishes which product it is. In parallel, near-infrared sensing reads the polymer and an inductive sensor detects metal, so the machine knows the material even if the label is damaged.

steps.title: [[RO]] Validate
steps.body: [[RO]] The read is checked against the register of deposit-bearing containers, and the container is checked for shape and emptiness. Anything unrecognised is handed straight back rather than swallowed.

steps.title: [[RO]] Return value
steps.body: [[RO]] Accepted containers are credited to the depositor at the machine — the reason they came. Value is redeemable in the store, which is what turns a return trip into a shopping trip.

steps.title: [[RO]] Sort by stream
steps.body: [[RO]] The container is diverted to its own path on the strength of the material read: PET one way, aluminium the other. Sorting happens here, before anything is crushed, because a compacted mixed mass cannot be separated.

steps.title: [[RO]] Compact
steps.body: [[RO]] Each stream is compacted its own way. PET is perforated and flattened so it cannot be re-inflated and claimed twice; cans are pressed flat. This is what makes a collection worth sending a vehicle for.

steps.title: [[RO]] Store
steps.body: [[RO]] Compacted material drops into a separate bin per stream, never a single mixed hopper. Fill level is monitored continuously, so a collection is scheduled against real volume rather than a calendar.

steps.title: [[RO]] Collect and report
steps.body: [[RO]] Green Exchange collects on a route driven by fill level. Every accepted container is already counted, so the site receives volumes by stream and machine availability without anyone tallying anything.

steps.title: [[RO]] Bale and offtake
steps.body: [[RO]] Material is baled by stream at a processing centre, not in the store, then sold to a reprocessor. Separation quality upstream is what the bale is priced on.
